sections_inspected: The supplied full text of BOURDIEU'S CLASS THEORY: The Academic as Revolutionary, especially pp. 109, 122, 134–136
scope_outcomes.criterion: A substantive passage must show Dylan Riley defending, reconstructing, criticizing, applying, or surveying a proposition associated with Max Weber.
scope_outcomes.basis: The text explicitly classifies Weber’s sociology of domination as a macrosociological theory, invokes Weber’s understanding of reflexive labor, and places Weber within the pluralist and mixed-constitution tradition used to assess Bourdieu.
limitations: This is one 2017 article and not Riley’s complete work.
The findings concern Riley’s demonstrated uses of Weber in this text, not a general ranking or overall assessment of his relationship to Weber.

evidence_state.coverage_basis: reader/reviewer report; source bytes do not establish inspection or completeness
blocking_issues: One or more declared finding references lack retained verified evidence
